---
title: "Plausibility checks for flight milestones"
subtitle: "Removing the milestones that the aircraft's own track contradicts, without removing correct ones"
author: "EUROCONTROL Performance Review Unit"
date: last-modified
---

```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(knitr)

# Read-only. Every number and table on this page comes from a CSV file in
# data/, staged by benchmarks/milestone_plausibility.py of the opdi
# repository. Nothing here reads S3, a database or a Spark cluster, and the
# page has no regeneration entrypoint: data/_manifest.json records, for each
# file, the script, its arguments, the git commit and the tables it read.
D <- function(f) read.csv(file.path("data", f), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

ba   <- D("before_after.csv")        # one row per event type, both runs
rem  <- D("removed_by_rule.csv")     # one row per check and event type, plus ALL
cand <- D("candidate_rules.csv")     # one row per candidate check, limit and type
ctx  <- D("context_by_type.csv")     # percentiles of the facts near each event
ex   <- D("examples.csv")            # removed events read by hand, 50 per check

num <- function(x, d = 0) formatC(as.numeric(x), format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")

# One number from each file, so that prose and tables cannot drift apart.
B  <- function(type, col) ba[ba$type == type, col]
R  <- function(rule, type, col) rem[rem$reject_rule == rule & rem$type == type, col]
C  <- function(rule, params, type, col) cand[cand$rule == rule & cand$params == params & cand$type == type, col]
X  <- function(type, subset, measure, col) ctx[ctx$type == type & ctx$subset == subset & ctx$measure == measure, col]
# The sum of one column of a candidate check over the event types the adopted
# check reads (the "ALL" rows of candidate_rules.csv also hold other types).
Cs <- function(rule, params, types, col) {
  sel <- cand[cand$rule == rule & cand$params == params & cand$type != "ALL", ]
  sum(sel[sel$type %in% types | (("layout" %in% types) & grepl("^(entry|exit)-", sel$type)), col])
}
RUNWAY_TIMES <- c("ATOT", "ALDT")
GROUND_EVENTS <- c("AOBT", "AIBT", "layout")   # "layout": every entry-/exit- type

MILESTONES <- c("AOBT", "AIBT", "ATOT", "ALDT")
confirmed_total <- sum(ba$confirmed_60s_before[ba$type %in% MILESTONES])
xing <- ba[startsWith(ba$type, "xing"), ]
events_before <- sum(ba$events_before)
events_after  <- sum(ba$events_after)

# The removed events read by hand.
ex_n <- function(rule, type) nrow(ex[ex$rule == rule & ex$type == type, ])
ex_first <- function(rule, type) {
  e <- ex[ex$rule == rule & ex$type == type, ]
  sum(e$event_time == e$trk_first_time, na.rm = TRUE)
}
```

## What was asked

OPDI publishes **milestones** of each flight: the off-block time (`AOBT`, the
aircraft leaves its stand), the take-off time (`ATOT`), the landing time
(`ALDT`), the in-block time (`AIBT`, the aircraft stops at its stand), and
many others. Each is found by a detector, a set of rules applied to the
position reports of one **track** (the reports that OPDI treats as one
flight).

Some published milestones could not be true: an in-block time while the
aircraft was still in the air, an off-block time after the take-off. The
question was: can such milestones be found and removed, without removing the
correct ones?

The answer is a set of five checks that compare each milestone with what the
aircraft's own position reports say it was doing at that time. This note
describes how the checks and their limits were chosen, and what they changed
on one day. The method itself is described on the methods page
[Plausibility checks](../../content/methods/plausibility-checks.qmd).

## Data

- **One worldwide day, 14 June 2026.** All `r num(events_before)` events of
  the day, computed with the default settings of the pipeline except the
  checks and the two detector rules described below. The tracks they come
  from were read again to find, for each event, what the aircraft was doing
  at that time.
- **Airport operator records** (APDF) of about ninety European airports for
  the same day. They hold `r num(B("AOBT", "records_on_day_before"))`
  off-block, `r num(B("ATOT", "records_on_day_before"))` take-off,
  `r num(B("ALDT", "records_on_day_before"))` landing and
  `r num(B("AIBT", "records_on_day_before"))` in-block times. An OPDI event is
  matched to the record of the same flight (same aircraft address, call sign
  and day) and the same milestone. It is **confirmed** when it is within 60 s
  of the record.

On that day, `r num(confirmed_total)` events were confirmed:
`r num(B("AOBT", "confirmed_60s_before"))` off-block,
`r num(B("AIBT", "confirmed_60s_before"))` in-block,
`r num(B("ATOT", "confirmed_60s_before"))` take-off and
`r num(B("ALDT", "confirmed_60s_before"))` landing times. These are the
events the checks must not remove.

For each event that a candidate check reads, the study took the facts from
the position reports of the same track within 60 s of the event: the height
above the airport (barometric altitude minus the airport's elevation), the
ground speed, and the share of reports flagged on the ground.

## How an implausible milestone arises

Reading the removed events one by one showed four patterns.

1. **A track first received in flight.** When the receivers first hear an
   aircraft after it has taken off, the first movement of the track is the
   flight itself. An off-block time read from the first movement of the whole
   track is then placed at the first report, thousands of feet above the
   departure airport. Of the `r ex_n("airborne_ground_event", "AOBT")`
   off-block times read by hand for the check "ground event while flying",
   `r ex_first("airborne_ground_event", "AOBT")` are at the first
   report of their track. The median height of all events read for that check
   is `r num(median(ex$ctx_height_ft[ex$rule == "airborne_ground_event"], na.rm = TRUE))` ft
   above the airport, at
   `r num(median(ex$ctx_speed_kt[ex$rule == "airborne_ground_event"], na.rm = TRUE))` kt.
2. **A track first received during the take-off.** The off-block time is then
   placed during the take-off roll or the first seconds of the climb, a few
   hundred feet above the airport and at about
   `r num(median(ex$ctx_speed_kt[ex$rule == "block_after_takeoff"], na.rm = TRUE))` kt,
   at or after the take-off time of the same track.
   `r ex_first("block_after_takeoff", "AOBT")` of the
   `r ex_n("block_after_takeoff", "AOBT")` examples read are at the
   first report of their track.
3. **An in-block time on the approach.** The in-block time was the end of the
   last movement anywhere in the track. In some tracks that movement ends on
   the final approach, so the in-block time is placed before the landing time,
   a few hundred feet above the airport, at about
   `r num(median(ex$ctx_speed_kt[ex$rule == "block_before_landing"], na.rm = TRUE))` kt.
4. **A crossing read from a report without a value.** Cleaning empties
   altitudes that cannot be trusted, so a track can hold reports with no
   altitude in the middle of a climb. A crossing of a flight level, of a
   distance ring or of the 15 ft height that defines a take-off or landing
   time, when it falls among such reports, got no time at all
   (`r num(sum(ba$without_time_before))` events of the day), or the time of
   another crossing of the same level or ring
   (`r num(sum(xing$crossings_sharing_time_before))` crossings).

Among the off-block and in-block times far from their record, the height
above the airport spreads to several thousand feet; among the confirmed ones
that have a known height, 95% are less than `r num(X("AOBT", "confirmed", "height_ft", "p95"))` ft
(off-block) and `r num(X("AIBT", "confirmed", "height_ft", "p95"))` ft
(in-block) above it. Most confirmed block times have no known height at all:
only `r num(X("AOBT", "confirmed", "height_ft", "n_known"))` of
`r num(X("AOBT", "confirmed", "height_ft", "n_events"))` confirmed off-block
times have a report with an altitude within 60 s, because reports sent on the
ground usually carry none.

## The checks and their limits

Each candidate check was measured on the events of the day with several
limits. A check was adopted only if it removed at most 0.1% of the confirmed
events, and only if it removes an event when every fact it needs is known.
An unknown fact keeps the event.

| Order | Check | Events read | Removed when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Event without a time | every type | it has no time |
| 2 | Ground event while flying | `AOBT`, `AIBT`, every entry into and exit from an airport area | more than 1,500 ft above the airport (more than 15,000 ft altitude when the airport is unknown), faster than 80 kt, and no report within 60 s flagged on the ground |
| 3 | Take-off or landing time too high | `ATOT`, `ALDT` | more than 1,500 ft above the airport |
| 4 | Off-block after take-off | `AOBT` | at or after the last `ATOT` of the track |
| 5 | In-block before landing | `AIBT` | at or before the first `ALDT` of the track |

### Height of the take-off and landing times

A take-off or landing time is the moment the aircraft passes 15 ft above the
airport, so a correct one is close to the ground. But a time some hundreds of
feet up is often still right: the barometric altitude is not corrected for
the local air pressure, and the reports around the moment are a few seconds
apart.

```{r tbl-runway-height}
#| echo: false
lims <- c(300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000)
p <- paste0("height_ft=", lims)
rt <- data.frame(
  limit = paste(num(lims), "ft"),
  removed = num(sapply(p, function(x) Cs("runway_time_too_high", x, RUNWAY_TIMES, "n_removed"))),
  confirmed = num(sapply(p, function(x) Cs("runway_time_too_high", x, RUNWAY_TIMES, "n_confirmed_removed"))),
  with_record = num(sapply(p, function(x) Cs("runway_time_too_high", x, RUNWAY_TIMES, "n_removed_with_record"))),
  far = num(sapply(p, function(x) Cs("runway_time_too_high", x, RUNWAY_TIMES, "n_removed_far_from_record")))
)
kable(rt, row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrr",
      col.names = c("Removed above", "Removed", "Of which confirmed", "With a record",
                    "More than 300 s from the record"),
      caption = paste0("Take-off and landing times (ATOT, ALDT) removed by a height limit, events of ",
                       "the day without the checks (",
                       num(Cs("runway_time_too_high", "height_ft=1500", RUNWAY_TIMES, "n_confirmed")),
                       " confirmed)."))
```

A limit of 1,000 ft or lower removes confirmed times. Between 1,000 and
1,500 ft, most of the times that have a record are confirmed by it:
`r num(Cs("runway_time_too_high", "height_ft=1000", RUNWAY_TIMES, "n_confirmed_removed") - Cs("runway_time_too_high", "height_ft=1500", RUNWAY_TIMES, "n_confirmed_removed"))`
of `r num(Cs("runway_time_too_high", "height_ft=1000", RUNWAY_TIMES, "n_removed_with_record") - Cs("runway_time_too_high", "height_ft=1500", RUNWAY_TIMES, "n_removed_with_record"))`.
Above 1,500 ft, no removed time is confirmed. The limit is therefore
1,500 ft.

### Ground events while flying

Height alone is not enough evidence for a ground event: some reports near the
ground carry a wrong altitude. The check therefore also requires a speed no
aircraft taxis at (80 kt; aircraft taxi at 10 to 30 kt) and no report in the
window flagged on the ground. When the airport is unknown, 15,000 ft of
altitude is used, which is above the highest airports in the world (about
14,500 ft).

```{r tbl-ground-event}
#| echo: false
rows <- list(
  c("1,500 ft", "height_ft=1500;speed_kt=None"),
  c("1,500 ft and 80 kt", "height_ft=1500;speed_kt=80"),
  c("1,500 ft, 80 kt and no report on the ground", "height_ft=1500;speed_kt=80;on_ground_max=0.0"),
  c("1,000 ft, 80 kt and no report on the ground", "height_ft=1000;speed_kt=80;on_ground_max=0.0"),
  c("2,000 ft, 80 kt and no report on the ground", "height_ft=2000;speed_kt=80;on_ground_max=0.0")
)
ge <- do.call(rbind, lapply(rows, function(r) data.frame(
  condition = r[1],
  removed = num(Cs("airborne_ground_event", r[2], GROUND_EVENTS, "n_removed")),
  confirmed = num(Cs("airborne_ground_event", r[2], GROUND_EVENTS, "n_confirmed_removed")),
  with_record = num(Cs("airborne_ground_event", r[2], GROUND_EVENTS, "n_removed_with_record")),
  far = num(Cs("airborne_ground_event", r[2], GROUND_EVENTS, "n_removed_far_from_record"))
)))
kable(ge, row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrr",
      col.names = c("Removed when above", "Removed", "Of which confirmed", "With a record",
                    "More than 300 s from the record"),
      caption = paste0("Off-block, in-block and airport area events removed by each condition, ",
                       "events of the day without the checks (",
                       num(Cs("airborne_ground_event", "height_ft=1500;speed_kt=80", GROUND_EVENTS, "n_confirmed")),
                       " confirmed block times)."))
```

Height alone removes confirmed block times; adding the speed and the
on-ground flag leaves two. Both are off-block times placed at the first
report of a track that was already about 3,000 ft above its departure
airport at more than 150 kt (they are in `data/examples.csv`). The aircraft
cannot have left its stand at that moment: the times match the record by
chance. The block-time rule described below no longer produces them, so the
check removes no confirmed time on the day. The limit of 1,500 ft is the same
as for the take-off and landing times.

### Order of the block times

An aircraft cannot leave its stand after it has taken off, nor reach its
stand before it has landed. Only times within one track are compared, and an
off-block time is compared with the **last** take-off of the track and an
in-block time with the **first** landing, so that a track that lands and
departs again keeps both its in-block and its off-block time.
Without the checks, an off-block time at or after the take-off was found for
`r num(C("block_after_takeoff", "tolerance_s=0", "AOBT", "n_removed"))`
events and an in-block time at or before the landing for
`r num(C("block_before_landing", "tolerance_s=0", "AIBT", "n_removed"))`;
none of them is confirmed.

## Two detector rules corrected at the same time

Two of the patterns above come from the detectors, and were corrected there.

- **Block times from the ground part of each leg.** The off-block and
  in-block times were taken from the first and last movement anywhere in the
  track, flight included. They are now read only from reports that may be on
  the ground (flagged on the ground, without altitude, or at most 2,000 ft
  above the airport), and only from the part of the track on the correct side
  of the take-off or landing. A track that lands and departs again gets the
  in-block time of its arrival and the off-block time of its departure.
- **Crossings over missing values.** A crossing is now placed between the last
  report with a known value and the first report with a known value after the
  crossing. When those two reports are more than 30 minutes apart, no crossing
  is given, because its time and position cannot be placed.

## Results

The day was computed again with the default settings: the five checks and the
two detector rules on. It then holds `r num(events_after)` events.

```{r tbl-removed}
#| echo: false
r <- rem[rem$reject_rule != "ALL", ]
agg <- aggregate(cbind(removed, removed_with_record, removed_confirmed_60s, removed_far_300s) ~ reject_rule,
                 data = r, FUN = sum)
names_rule <- c(airborne_ground_event = "Ground event while flying",
                runway_time_too_high = "Take-off or landing time too high",
                block_after_takeoff = "Off-block after take-off",
                block_before_landing = "In-block before landing")
agg <- agg[match(names(names_rule), agg$reject_rule), ]
tot <- rem[rem$reject_rule == "ALL", ]
tab <- data.frame(
  check = c(names_rule[agg$reject_rule], "All checks"),
  removed = num(c(agg$removed, tot$removed)),
  with_record = num(c(agg$removed_with_record, tot$removed_with_record)),
  confirmed = num(c(agg$removed_confirmed_60s, tot$removed_confirmed_60s)),
  far = num(c(agg$removed_far_300s, tot$removed_far_300s))
)
kable(tab, row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrr",
      col.names = c("Check", "Removed", "With a record", "Confirmed", "More than 300 s from the record"),
      caption = "Events removed by each check with the default settings, 14 June 2026.")
```

The checks removed `r num(R("ALL", "ALL", "removed"))` events. Of the
`r num(R("ALL", "ALL", "removed_with_record"))` that have a record,
`r num(R("ALL", "ALL", "removed_far_300s"))` are more than 300 s from it, and
`r num(R("ALL", "ALL", "removed_confirmed_60s"))` is within 60 s: **no
confirmed milestone was removed**. No event was removed for having no time,
because the crossing rule gives every crossing a time or no crossing at all.

```{r tbl-before-after}
#| echo: false
# Columns are named <measure>_before and <measure>_after, with "_pct" after
# them for the shares.
row <- function(label, col, d = 0, unit = "", suffix = "") {
  v <- unlist(lapply(MILESTONES, function(t)
    c(B(t, paste0(col, "_before", suffix)), B(t, paste0(col, "_after", suffix)))))
  c(label, paste0(num(v, d), unit))
}
cols <- c(sapply(MILESTONES, function(t) c(paste(t, "off"), paste(t, "default"))))
m <- rbind(
  c("Events", num(unlist(lapply(MILESTONES, function(t) c(B(t, "events_before"), B(t, "events_after")))))),
  row("Records with an OPDI time (coverage)", "coverage", 2, "%", "_pct"),
  row("Within 60 s of the record", "share_60s", 2, "%", "_pct"),
  row("Within 300 s of the record", "share_300s", 2, "%", "_pct"),
  row("90th percentile of the absolute difference", "p90_abs_error_s", 0, " s"),
  row("Confirmed events", "confirmed_60s", 0, "")
)
kable(m, row.names = FALSE, align = c("l", rep("r", 8)),
      col.names = c("", cols),
      caption = paste("The four milestones against the airport records, with the checks and the",
                      "two detector rules off and with the default settings."))
```

Fewer off-block and in-block times are published: coverage of the records
falls from `r num(B("AOBT", "coverage_before_pct"), 2)`% to
`r num(B("AOBT", "coverage_after_pct"), 2)`% for `AOBT` and from
`r num(B("AIBT", "coverage_before_pct"), 2)`% to
`r num(B("AIBT", "coverage_after_pct"), 2)`% for `AIBT`, because wrong times
are no longer published. Those that remain are closer to the records: within
60 s, `r num(B("AOBT", "share_60s_before_pct"), 1)`% →
`r num(B("AOBT", "share_60s_after_pct"), 1)`% and
`r num(B("AIBT", "share_60s_before_pct"), 1)`% →
`r num(B("AIBT", "share_60s_after_pct"), 1)`%; the 90th percentile of the
absolute difference falls from `r num(B("AOBT", "p90_abs_error_s_before"))` s
to `r num(B("AOBT", "p90_abs_error_s_after"))` s and from
`r num(B("AIBT", "p90_abs_error_s_before"))` s to
`r num(B("AIBT", "p90_abs_error_s_after"))` s.

The number of confirmed events did not fall for any milestone. Of the
`r num(B("AOBT", "confirmed_60s_before"))` confirmed off-block times of the
first run, `r num(B("AOBT", "confirmed_before_same_time_after"))` are
published again at the same time. The
`r num(B("AOBT", "confirmed_60s_before") - B("AOBT", "confirmed_before_same_time_after"))`
others are off-block times that were placed at the first report of a track
already in flight and matched a record by chance; the ground-part rule does
not produce them. Of the `r num(B("AIBT", "confirmed_60s_before"))` confirmed
in-block times, `r num(B("AIBT", "confirmed_before_same_time_after"))` are
published again at the same time.

The crossing rule gave a time to `r num(sum(ba$null_now_timed))` crossings
that had none, and gave no crossing in
`r num(sum(ba$null_not_emitted))` cases, where the two known values are more
than 30 minutes apart. These include the crossings of the 15 ft height that
define `r num(B("ATOT", "null_before"))` take-off and
`r num(B("ALDT", "null_before"))` landing times. The
`r num(sum(xing$crossings_sharing_time_before))` crossings that carried the
time of another crossing no longer do.

## What was not adopted

```{r tbl-not-adopted}
#| echo: false
na_rows <- list(
  c("Taxi time too long: take-off minus off-block, or in-block minus landing", "minutes=30", "30 min"),
  c("", "minutes=60", "60 min"),
  c("", "minutes=180", "180 min"),
  c("Lower height limit for take-off and landing times", "height_ft=1000", "1,000 ft"),
  c("", "height_ft=500", "500 ft"),
  c("Take-off after landing in one track: remove the take-off", "remove=ATOT", ""),
  c("Take-off after landing in one track: remove the landing", "remove=ALDT", ""),
  c("Distance from the airport", "distance_nm=3", "3 NM"),
  c("", "distance_nm=5", "5 NM"),
  c("", "distance_nm=20", "20 NM"),
  c("Ground event faster than a speed, whatever its height", "speed_kt=80", "80 kt"),
  c("", "speed_kt=150", "150 kt")
)
rule_of <- c("Taxi" = "taxi_too_long", "Lower" = "runway_time_too_high", "Take-off" = "takeoff_after_landing",
             "Distance" = "far_from_airport", "Ground" = "ground_event_speed_only")
# A height limit for runway times is counted over ATOT and ALDT only; the
# other candidates over every type they read (their "ALL" row).
value <- function(rule, params, col) {
  if (rule == "runway_time_too_high") Cs(rule, params, RUNWAY_TIMES, col) else C(rule, params, "ALL", col)
}
current <- ""
na <- do.call(rbind, lapply(na_rows, function(r) {
  if (r[1] != "") current <<- rule_of[[strsplit(r[1], " ")[[1]][1]]]
  data.frame(
    check = r[1], limit = r[3],
    removed = num(value(current, r[2], "n_removed")),
    confirmed = paste0(num(value(current, r[2], "n_confirmed_removed")), " of ",
                       num(value(current, r[2], "n_confirmed"))),
    far = num(value(current, r[2], "n_removed_far_from_record"))
  )
}))
kable(na, row.names = FALSE, align = "llrrr",
      col.names = c("Candidate check", "Limit", "Removed", "Confirmed removed",
                    "More than 300 s from the record"),
      caption = "Candidate checks that were not adopted, events of the day without the checks.")
```

- **Taxi time too long.** It removes confirmed times at every limit tried,
  from 30 min to 180 min. A long taxi time is unusual, not impossible.
- **A lower height limit for take-off and landing times.** It removes
  confirmed times: `r num(Cs("runway_time_too_high", "height_ft=1000", RUNWAY_TIMES, "n_confirmed_removed"))`
  at 1,000 ft and `r num(Cs("runway_time_too_high", "height_ft=500", RUNWAY_TIMES, "n_confirmed_removed"))`
  at 500 ft.
- **Take-off after landing in one track.** Such a track often holds a real
  arrival followed by a real departure of the same aircraft. Removing the
  take-off time removes `r num(C("takeoff_after_landing", "remove=ATOT", "ALL", "n_confirmed_removed"))`
  confirmed ones, removing the landing time
  `r num(C("takeoff_after_landing", "remove=ALDT", "ALL", "n_confirmed_removed"))`.
- **Distance from the airport.** At 3 NM it removes confirmed take-off and
  landing times; at 5 to 20 NM it still removes confirmed in-block times.
  Combined with a height of more than 1,000 ft it removes no confirmed time,
  but it then describes an aircraft in flight, which check 2 already covers.
- **Speed alone.** It removes confirmed block times at every speed tried:
  `r num(C("ground_event_speed_only", "speed_kt=80", "ALL", "n_confirmed_removed"))`
  at 80 kt and `r num(C("ground_event_speed_only", "speed_kt=150", "ALL", "n_confirmed_removed"))`
  at 150 kt. Speed is therefore used only together with the height and the
  on-ground flag.

Checks on the tops of climb and descent, on level segments and on the
distance rings were also measured. A top of descent before the top of climb
never occurred (`r num(C("top_order", "", "ALL", "n_removed"))` of
`r num(C("top_order", "", "ALL", "n_events"))` tops). The other candidates
remove events that no airport record covers, so whether they remove right
events cannot be judged. None was adopted.

## Limits

- The limits rest on one day and on the records of about ninety European
  airports. Elsewhere and on other days, the share of right events removed has
  not been measured.
- The checks only remove events. They do not correct a wrong time or find a
  missing one, so the coverage of the block times falls.
- An event that the track does not contradict is kept even when it is wrong,
  for example a block time a few minutes off.
- A `landing` event (the passage over the runway threshold) is not checked:
  one in twenty is more than `r num(X("landing", "all", "height_ft", "p95"))` ft
  above the airport, and it is left as it is.
- Tops of climb and descent, level segments, holding, point merge, FIR
  crossings and go-arounds have no check other than the missing time.
- A block time still needs the track to pass a stand somewhere.
- The airport surface events accept reports up to 2,000 ft above the airport;
  check 2 removes what that lets through only when the aircraft is also
  faster than 80 kt and has no report on the ground.

## Provenance

Every number and table on this page is read from the CSV files in `data/`
when the page is rendered; nothing is computed on a cluster. The files were
written by `benchmarks/milestone_plausibility.py` of the opdi repository.
`data/_manifest.json` records, for each file, the command and its arguments,
the git commit, whether the working copy had uncommitted changes, a
fingerprint of the source files, and the input tables with their size and
date. `candidate_rules.csv`, `context_by_type.csv`, `sequence_by_flight.csv`
and `examples.csv` describe the events of the day without the checks;
`before_after.csv` and `removed_by_rule.csv` compare them with the run with
the default settings.
